q: Which questions make the Assistant look at the picture?
a: Questions about the picture itself: exposure, colour, skin, sky, light, once the picture model is installed. Then Revolution renders the Program frame small and the vision model writes one or two sentences about what it sees that bears on your question (for example the sky shifts from purple to orange at the horizon, low sun); the assistant gets that line with the measured numbers. How-to questions (how do I add a node?) skip it.

q: Where is the Picture model setting?
a: Settings ▸ Color, under AI explanations: Picture model (Qwen3-VL 4B Instruct, about 8.9 GB, Apache-2.0). Download (`ai.vision.download`) fetches it from the publisher's Hugging Face page at a fixed version and checks every file against its checksum; Cancel download stops it; the row says installed when done (`ai.vision.status`); Remove (`ai.vision.remove`) deletes it again.

q: Why was the first picture look so slow?
a: The very first look prepares the model: about 25 seconds and a 4.3 GB file next to it. After that a look takes about 1–2 seconds on a separate graphics card (after several seconds of loading) or about 8–30 seconds on the processor with only built-in graphics.

q: Does the vision model stay in memory?
a: For two minutes after a look, so follow-up questions don't load it again; then the memory is freed. While it looks it needs about 10 GB of free memory.

q: I asked what would you do with this shot; did it look again?
a: No new look: a later question about the shot that isn't about exposure, colour or skin gets the last look of that shot, if there is one. Asking the same question about the same frame also reuses the look. Changing the clip's grade or effects makes it a new shot.

q: Does the picture model send my frames to the cloud?
a: No. It runs on your computer and nothing leaves it; Revolution downloads the model once (from the publisher's Hugging Face page) and checks it, then every look is local.

q: Does Remove also delete files I put in the picture model's folder?
a: No. Remove (`ai.vision.remove`) deletes the picture model and the text model prepared from it; other files you put in its folder stay.

q: What does the Assistant know about my shot without the picture model?
a: With each question it is told which clips are selected and, when the selected clip has a grade, what its current node does to the frame under the playhead, measured from the picture. It also gets a short measured fact sheet of that frame before and after the grade: where the mids sit against middle grey, clipping and crushing, contrast, the colour of near-neutral areas, saturation, and how much of the frame has skin-tone colours, plus whether the clip is log footage. These are numbers turned into words; the picture model adds a look at the frame itself.

q: Can the Assistant tell a face from a wooden table?
a: From the measured fact sheet alone, no: skin-tone colours are numbers turned into words, so they can be a sunset or a wooden table, not only a face. With the picture model installed, picture questions also get a look at the frame itself, which can say what it actually sees.

q: And how long will I wait for that on a PC without a graphics card?
a: With only the graphics built into the processor, the picture model runs on the processor: about 8–30 seconds a look, and the answer starts that much later. With a separate graphics card (AMD Radeon, NVIDIA GeForce, Intel Arc) a look takes about 1–2 seconds after several seconds of loading. The first look ever also prepares the model (about 25 seconds).

q: ok I regraded it, ask again
a: Changing the clip's grade or effects counts as a new shot, so a picture question now gets a fresh look at the regraded frame rather than reusing the old one. If the model was used in the last two minutes it is still loaded, so the look starts quicker.

context.q: why does my sky look purple at the top
context.a: The picture look says the sky shifts from purple to orange at the horizon with a low sun; the measured facts show the near-neutral areas leaning magenta.
